Benzene.toxic_gas_emission: Carbon monoxide, toxic aromatic vapors, dense black carcinogenic soot
Benzene.suppression_agent: Alcohol-resistant Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AR-AFFF) or dry chemical powder. NEVER use high-pressure solid water stream which scatters burning liquid.
Benzene.protective_equipment: Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) Level A fully encapsulating chemical protective suit.

Liquefied Petroleum Gas.toxic_gas_emission: Unburned hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide. Extreme BLEVE (Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapor Explosion) hazard if vessel exposed to flame.
Liquefied Petroleum Gas.suppression_agent: Do NOT extinguish leaking gas fire unless leak can be stopped immediately. Use massive water deluge monitors to cool tank shell from maximum distance.
Liquefied Petroleum Gas.protective_equipment: Thermal protective firefighting turnout gear with SCBA and explosive atmosphere gas detectors.

Anhydrous Ammonia.toxic_gas_emission: Highly pungent, suffocating toxic vapor plume (IDLH 300 ppm). Reacts with atmospheric moisture to form dense white corrosive aerosol clouds.
Anhydrous Ammonia.suppression_agent: Deploy high-volume water fog / curtain monitors downwind to scrub vapor from air. Do NOT put water directly inside ammonia storage tanks.
Anhydrous Ammonia.protective_equipment: Level A gas-tight chemical suit with positive-pressure SCBA.

Chlorine Gas.toxic_gas_emission: Yellow-green suffocating gas, 2.5x heavier than air (pools in low-lying trenches). Powerful oxidizer causing rapid explosion of combustibles.
Chlorine Gas.suppression_agent: Never spray water directly on chlorine leak. Use alkaline scrubber systems or spray water curtains to knock down dispersing cloud.
Chlorine Gas.protective_equipment: Level A encapsulating suit, continuous electrochemical chlorine sensors.

Crude Oil.toxic_gas_emission: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S), sulfur dioxide, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, boilover hazard in open-top tanks.
Crude Oil.suppression_agent: Sub-surface or topside Class B AFFF foam pourers. Rim seal fire protection system. Cool adjacent storage tanks with water spray.
Crude Oil.protective_equipment: Fire proximity suit with H2S gas detection monitor.

Ethylene.toxic_gas_emission: Carbon monoxide, rapid vapor cloud explosion (VCE) risk if confined.
Ethylene.suppression_agent: Shut off fuel feed. Cool vessel walls with fixed water monitors. Dry chemical or carbon dioxide for small manifold fires.
Ethylene.protective_equipment: Full structural firefighting gear and positive-pressure SCBA.

Industrial Accidental Fire: Phase 1: Immediate isolation of hydrocarbon / chemical feed lines within 90 seconds of detection.
Phase 2: Automated activation of fixed deluge spray systems and perimeter foam monitors.
Phase 3: Sound Facility Emergency Siren (Continuous 3-minute oscillating tone) and notify Local District Emergency Operations Center (DEOC).
Phase 4: Establish Incident Command Post upwind and outside the minimum 1.5 km thermal radiation threshold (4.75 kW/m²).
Phase 5: Deploy Mutual Aid Scheme (neighboring industrial units) for backup foam concentrate supply.
Phase 6: Continuous atmospheric gas monitoring downwind for toxic combustion byproducts (CO, H2S, VOCs).
Gas Flare Anomalous Spike: Step 1: Check flare knock-out drum liquid level to rule out hydrocarbon carryover.
Step 2: Verify steam injection ratio / purge gas flow to restore smokeless flaring combustion.
Step 3: Inspect upstream relief valves for stuck-open bypass or emergency pressure venting.
Wildfire Boundary Interception: Step 1: Create a 50-meter clear mineral firebreak along the industrial plant perimeter fence.
Step 2: Turn on facility exterior water wall monitors to prevent ember ignition of exterior fuel storage tanks.
Step 3: Coordinate with State Forest Department and Fire Services for back-burning and aerial water drops.
